critique.evidence: The screen directly advances the defense-economics story by comparing before/after attack cost, fraud success, cost per successful fraud, and attacker ROI across all viewports. However, it does not establish Mastercard-specific relevance: there is no connection to card-payment actors, transaction flows, issuer/merchant losses, authorization integrity, or network-scale impact. The central claim also overreaches the shown result—post-defense attacker ROI remains 25.60× and is explicitly labeled above break-even, so the evidence shows reduced profitability rather than a defense that “wins the campaign.” Denominators, fraud-value assumptions, time window, and provenance are absent, limiting credibility as a results artifact.
critique.fix: Tie the ledger to a concrete Mastercard payment scenario and identify affected stakeholders and transaction stage. Show attack volume, evaluation window, fraud-value and cost assumptions, avoided fraud loss, false-positive/customer-friction cost, defender ROI, and uncertainty. Reframe the conclusion as economic pressure unless the measured post-defense ROI falls below break-even, or demonstrate the additional controls needed to reach deterrence.
